priceCaption: Base specification price, customisations quoted separately.
opener: A prefab labour camp is the relocatable build in the SAMAN worker housing family: bolted light-steel panels on pedestal footings, with repeatable door and window modules and plug-and-play electrical blocks, so the same camp dismantles and re-erects at the next project. Blocks arrange around a central services spine to the approved site plan. Sizes span 60x24 ft G+1 through 120x24 ft G+2 for 58 to 216 workers a building, each priced ex-factory on the camp's own square-foot rate with a fixed quote in 48 hours.
descriptionHtml:
Most worker housing is written off when the project ends. The prefab labour camp is engineered so it is not: wall, floor and roof panels share one bolted module, the whole block stands on pedestal pads instead of a poured slab, and electrical blocks plug together through external cable trays. When the project finishes, the camp unbolts, travels on trailers, panels numbered for reassembly, and stands again at the next site far faster than it first went up.

That mobility changes the arithmetic. Rate for rate a camp runs a little above a fixed open-hall shed of the same size, and repays the difference the first time it moves. Across three projects the same block becomes the cheapest housing a contractor owns. Pedestal footings also mean leaving a site means lifting pads, never breaking concrete, so ground reinstatement takes days and deposits come back.

The blocks group along a single services spine carrying ring-main water and zoned power, and repeat customers carry one block numbering from site to site so the layout plan follows the buildings with the buildings. Crews wanting lockable rooms in a movable block should compare the room-block hutment first. If your work is one long project on one site, the full colony line-up shows the fixed buildings that cost less for the same area. If your projects move, this is the building that moves with them.
